questions.q: According to the DOH guidelines for patient movement, corridors designed for access by patients and equipment must maintain a absolute minimum clear width of how many meters?
o: 2.44 meters
1.83 meters
2.00 meters
2.50 meters
questions.n: This is the exact statutory requirement for primary institutional corridors accommodating patient beds, stretchers, and equipment movement.

questions.q: In areas within a hospital or healthcare facility that are not commonly used for bed, stretcher, and equipment transport, corridors may be reduced to a minimum width of:
o: 1.50 meters
1.83 meters
1.22 meters
2.10 meters
questions.n: The guidelines explicitly state that secondary corridors not subjected to heavy patient transport equipment can be reduced to 1.83 meters.

questions.q: What architectural circulation features must be explicitly provided to connect ancillary, clinical, and nursing areas located on an upper floor?
o: Fire-rated stairwells and dumbwaiters
Ramps and standard service stairs
An elevator and escalator system
A ramp or elevator
questions.n: The text explicitly requires either a functional ramp or an elevator system to secure direct vertical mobility between these crucial medical zones.

questions.q: When a main hospital entrance is constructed and positioned not on the same level of the site, what specific design feature must be integrated?
o: A ramp
Steps with nosing
A mechanical lift
An escalator
questions.n: A ramp must be provided to bridge the grade discrepancy and guarantee unbroken, wheel-accessible admission into the facility.

questions.q: Under Section 4 (Security), a hospital and other health facilities shall ensure the security of person and property for which distinct groups within the facility?
o: Doctors, nurses, and medical technicians
Patients, medical staff, and administration
Patients, personnel, and public
Inpatients, outpatients, and watchers
questions.n: The code explicitly dictates that security measures must comprehensive protect all three categories of occupants.

questions.q: Hospital illumination guidelines state that all areas must be provided with sufficient lighting to achieve what multi-faceted objective?
o: To reduce electrical consumption, prevent glare, and maintain architectural visual design consistency.
To eliminate shadows in diagnostic suites and maximize brightness inside administrative and public spaces.
To promote comfort, healing, and recovery of patients, and to enable personnel in the performance of work.
To enhance the visibility of emergency exits and maintain constant illumination in critical patient wards.
questions.n: This verbatim response accurately captures the clinical and functional goals assigned to lighting systems in health environments.

questions.q: What is the primary objective specified under Section 7 for providing adequate ventilation within a hospital or health facility?
o: To control airborne pathogens and eliminate chemical odors from laboratories.
To regulate humidity levels and reduce the overall building heat load.
To maintain negative air pressure zones inside isolation wards.
To ensure comfort of patients, personnel and public.
questions.n: The text simplifies the core intent of ventilation to establishing environmental comfort for all users.

questions.q: To satisfy Section 8 (Auditory and Visual Privacy), what metrics must a hospital observe to achieve the necessary environment for unhampered conduct of activities?
o: Decibel attenuation scales and physical separation distances
Acceptable sound level and adequate visual seclusion
Acoustic buffer zones and opaque partition walls
Sound transmission class ratings and window blinds
questions.n: The guidelines pair acoustic limits with visual isolation to define the absolute privacy envelope within clinical areas.

questions.q: Regarding Section 9 (Water Supply), what specific criteria must the approved public water supply system fulfill at all times?
o: The water supply must be chemically neutral, pressurized, filtered, and monitored by daily testing regimes.
The system must utilize redundant storage tanks, copper distribution lines, and backup booster pumps.
The water supply shall be potable, safe for drinking and adequate, and shall be brought into the building free of cross connections.
The supply must be chlorinated, high-volume, cost-efficient, and derived from local artesian sources.
questions.n: This complete definition guarantees chemical/biological safety, volume availability, and mechanical system isolation.

questions.q: Section 10 mandates that liquid waste and solid waste must be managed through what specific channels?
o: Liquid waste neutralized via holding tanks; solid waste transported directly to regional sanitary landfills.
Liquid waste processed through grease traps; solid waste sorted into hazardous and non-hazardous collection bins.
Liquid waste directed to on-site treatment plants; solid waste compressed and incinerated within the medical facility.
Liquid waste discharged into an approved public sewerage system; solid waste collected, treated and disposed of in accordance with applicable codes.
questions.n: This accurately reflects the dual-track system required for municipal liquid disposal and legal solid waste containment/treatment.

questions.q: Under Section 11 (Sanitation), what utilities must be provided through the buildings and premises to ensure a clean and healthy environment?
o: Storm drainage networks and dedicated solid waste chutes
Hot water loops, medical gas lines, and clinical drains
Centralized vacuum systems and automated greywater filtration
Approved water supply and sewerage system
questions.n: These two infrastructural utilities form the basic foundation required to maintain sanitation standards throughout the facility.

questions.q: What type of environment is housekeeping specifically mandated to provide and maintain for patients, personnel, and the public?
o: An aseptic and hazard-free environment
A healthy and aesthetic environment
A pristine and allergen-controlled environment
A sterile and clinically odorless environment
questions.n: The framework specifically pairs physical health safety with visual/spatial aesthetics as the core baseline for housekeeping.

questions.q: What is the stated objective of implementing an effective building maintenance program for buildings and equipment?
o: To comply with insurance policies and building management system logs.
To lower operational overhead and minimize utility bills.
To extend the real estate value and modernize clinical infrastructure.
To prevent untimely breakdown of buildings and equipment.
questions.n: The regulations clarify that the core focus of the program is preventing premature system and structural degradation.

questions.q: Section 14 dictates that floors, walls, and ceilings shall be composed of sturdy materials that allow for which three performance attributes?
o: Asepsis, impact insulation, and seamless installation.
Light reflection, slip resistance, and modular replacement.
Durability, ease of cleaning, and fire resistance.
Sound absorption, scratch resistance, and waterproofing.
questions.n: These three exact specifications guarantee that surfaces resist degradation, prevent bacterial buildup, and maintain fire safety containment.

questions.q: Under Section 15 (Segregation), what is the mandatory toilet-to-patient/personnel ratio required within separate facilities for wards?
o: One (1) toilet for every ten (10) patients or personnel
One (1) toilet for every eight (8) patients or personnel
One (1) toilet for every twelve (12) patients or personnel
One (1) toilet for every five (5) patients or personnel
questions.n: This is the precise prescriptive numerical ratio mandated for sanitation fixtures within segregated ward zones.

questions.q: Section 16 categorizes fire protection into two distinct systemic approaches. What specific elements are explicitly named for each?
o: Measures for detecting fire (fire alarms, peepholes, smoke detectors) and devices for quenching fire (fire extinguishers, fire hoses).
Heat sensors, fire hydrants, specialized kitchen hoods, and automated chemical deluge systems.
Flame retardant curtains, fire doors, and pressurized exit stairs with illuminated exit directional signage.
Passive fire barriers (intumescent paint, fire dampers) and active fire suppression systems (automatic fire sprinklers).
questions.n: This directly reflects the text's division between fire detection measures and fire quenching devices located in strategic areas.

questions.q: What is the comprehensive definition of an effective graphic system (Signage) under Section 17?
o: A standardized set of bilingual labels applied onto walls to designate emergency egress doors and restrict unauthorized room entries.
Illuminated wayfinding directories placed at major corridor intersections to help outpatients find clinical spaces.
Universal pictograms and symbols color-coded to differentiate medical departments from public support zones.
A number of individual visual aids and devices arranged to provide information, orientation, direction, identification, prohibition, warning and official notice.
questions.n: This complete statement outlines the entire functional spectrum required for a graphic communication system within a health facility.

questions.q: What is the minimum required parking space allocation for a hospital or health facility based on bed capacity?
o: Minimum of one (1) parking space for every twenty-five (25) beds
Minimum of one (1) parking space for every ten (10) beds
Minimum of one (1) parking space for every thirty (30) beds
Minimum of one (1) parking space for every fifty (50) beds
questions.n: The prescriptive zoning guideline dictates a minimum ratio of 1 stall per 25 patient beds.

questions.q: Areas that are immediately accessible to the public, such as emergency service, outpatient service, and administrative service, are grouped into which zone?
o: Outer Zone
Deep Zone
Second Zone
Inner Zone
questions.n: The Outer Zone is designated for the most public-facing, high-turnover entry functions that require close proximity to the hospital perimeter.

questions.q: The laboratory, pharmacy, and radiology departments receive workload from the outer zone and must be located near it. What zone do these belong to?
o: Deep Zone
Service Zone
Second Zone
Inner Zone
questions.n: The Second Zone functions as an intermediary diagnostic and pharmaceutical support level that interfaces directly with the outer public zones.

questions.q: What zone consists of areas that provide nursing care and management of patients, and must be located in private areas but accessible to guests?
o: Inner Zone
Outer Zone
Deep Zone
Second Zone
questions.n: The Inner Zone encompasses nursing wards and patient care spaces, balancing patient privacy with necessary visitor access.

questions.q: Areas that require asepsis to perform prescribed services—such as surgical service, delivery service, nursery, and intensive care—are classified under which zone?
o: Second Zone
Service Zone
Inner Zone
Deep Zone
questions.n: The Deep Zone requires strict environmental controls and high sterility to isolate high-risk surgical and critical care interventions.

questions.q: Dietary service, housekeeping, maintenance, motorpool, and the mortuary belong to which zone, and how must they be positioned relative to traffic?
o: Deep Zone; located adjacent to the surgical suites.
Second Zone; located near the diagnostic departments.
Outer Zone; located near the front entry gates.
Service Zone; located in areas away from normal traffic.
questions.n: The Service Zone handles utility and back-of-house support operations, requiring isolation from main patient and visitor pathways.

questions.q: Section 20.1 dictates that the emergency service must be located on the ground floor for immediate access. What additional entrance feature is required?
o: A separate entrance to the emergency room shall be provided.
A secure portal connecting directly through the administrative suite.
An exclusive access ramp connecting to the underground parking deck.
A shared entrance with the outpatient department clinic.
questions.n: A dedicated entrance ensures that critical emergency transport avoids congestion at the main public lobby.

questions.q: Regarding administrative services, where must the admitting and business offices be located, and where can the hospital management offices be situated?
o: Admitting and business offices in the Service Zone; management offices adjacent to the emergency room.
Admitting and business offices on upper floors; management offices in the central public courtyard.
Admitting and business offices in the Deep Zone; management offices near the front entrance.
Admitting and business offices near the main entrance; management offices in private areas.
questions.n: This places public transaction areas right at the front entry while keeping administrative leadership offices in quieter, low-traffic areas.

questions.q: To maintain proper asepsis, how must the surgical service suite be arranged, and how must its dressing room be positioned?
o: Operating room connected directly to the mortuary; dressing room opening directly into the cafeteria.
Operating room directly facing the main corridor; dressing room positioned open to the public lounge.
Operating room integrated into the outpatient zone; dressing room shared with the service zone workforce.
Operating room as remote as practicable from the entrance; dressing room located to avoid exposure to dirty areas after changing.
questions.n: This layout protects the sterile field by keeping the operating room clear of cross-traffic and ensuring staff don't re-contaminate themselves after changing into surgical scrubs.

questions.q: The design criteria for the delivery service suite mirror the surgical suite regarding traffic separation and dressing room paths. What is the specific requirement for the nursery?
o: The nursery must be combined with the pediatric outpatient consultation rooms.
The nursery must be integrated inside the main public waiting room.
The nursery shall be separate but immediately accessible from the delivery room.
The nursery shall be located on an alternate floor accessible only via public elevators.
questions.n: This ensures a quick, secure transport path for newborns from delivery directly into a dedicated care space without traveling down public corridors.

questions.q: Section 20.5 requires that a nurse station be provided in all inpatient units of the hospital with a minimum ratio of:
o: At least one (1) nurse station for every twenty (20) beds
At least one (1) nurse station for every hundred (100) beds
At least one (1) nurse station for every fifty (50) beds
At least one (1) nurse station for every thirty-five (35) beds
questions.n: This prescriptive ratio ensures that nursing staff can effectively monitor, supervise, and respond to their assigned inpatient beds.

questions.q: What is the minimum required separation distance between the dietary service and the hospital morgue?
o: At least 15-meter distance
At least 25-meter distance
At least 50-meter distance
At least 10-meter distance
questions.n: This minimum horizontal separation is required to prevent cross-contamination and maintain sanitation between food preparation and the mortuary.

questions.q: Section 21 establishes a general rule for space planning. What must an adequate area accommodate within a hospital layout?
o: The clear structural grid lines, columns, and partition wall thicknesses.
The mechanical ducts, electrical panels, and cable trays.
The future expansion capability, floor-to-ceiling heights, and window openings.
The people, activity, furniture, equipment and utility.
questions.n: This core space planning rule requires that rooms be sized to accommodate occupants, their movements, furnishings, clinical machinery, and utility connections.

questions.q: According to Note 1 on the dimensional criteria chart, the value of 0.65/person represents:
o: Unit area per person occupying the space at one time
The structural thickness factor allowed for interior partition walls
Clear circulation clearance width inside patient rooms
The average width of an standard outpatient wheelchair
questions.n: This metric defines the baseline floor area required for a single standing occupant in a shared room.

questions.q: The planning value of 5.02/staff defines the work area per staff member. What specific elements must be accommodated within this area?
o: Space for two filing cabinets, a computer terminal, and a personal locker module
Space for one (1) desk and one (1) chair, space for occasional visitor, and space for aisle
Space for a rolling medication cart, a computer-on-wheels, and staff seating
Space for a medical examination table, a sink counter, and waste disposal bins
questions.n: This spatial formula ensures that administrative and clinical workstations have enough room for a desk, seating, guest access, and clear foot traffic pathways.

questions.q: Note 3 specifies an alternate unit area index of 1.40/person. This value defines:
o: Unit area per person occupying the space at one time
The space multiplier for outdoor waiting plazas
The clear width required for single-file exit doors
The minimum space required for a person using a walker
questions.n: This larger metric provides an expanded per-person area allocation, typically used for more spacious occupancy or waiting layouts.

questions.q: What is the required clear floor area per bed, and what three functional spaces must be included within that footprint?
o: 6.50/bed; includes space for a bed, an intravenous stand pole, and a doctor's examination stool
10.00/bed; includes space for a patient bed, private washroom, and nurse documentation desk
5.00/bed; includes space for one (1) bed, a bedside table, and a built-in wardrobe closet
7.43/bed; includes space for one (1) bed, space for occasional visitor, and space for passage of equipment
questions.n: This specific area allocation ensures there is enough room for the patient bed, visitor seating, and the safe movement of medical equipment around the bedside.

questions.q: According to Note 5, what is the required clear floor area per stretcher to accommodate a single stretcher unit?
o: 1.50/stretcher
0.90/stretcher
1.08/stretcher
2.00/stretcher
questions.n: This precise area index defines the minimum spatial footprint required to park or position a standard medical stretcher.

questions.q: A design team is developing a 140-bed general hospital. To comply with the mandated nursing unit ratios under Section 20.5, how many nurse stations must be programmed?
o: Exactly 5 nurse stations
Exactly 2 nurse stations
Exactly 3 nurse stations
Exactly 4 nurse stations
questions.n:
Dividing 140 beds by the maximum ratio of 35 beds per station requires exactly 4 stations (

questions.q: During spatial programming, the project architect must locate the laboratory, pharmacy, and radiology departments. According to functional hospital zoning, how should they be positioned relative to the emergency and administrative services?
o: They belong to the Second Zone and must be located near the Outer Zone to process its incoming workload.
They belong to the Deep Zone and must be completely isolated from the Outer Zone.
They belong to the Inner Zone and should be interspersed within private inpatient wards.
They belong to the Service Zone and should be located next to the mortuary and loading dock.
questions.n: This follows the sequential zoning flow, placing second-zone diagnostic services adjacent to high-traffic outer public zones.

questions.q: You are designing a surgical wing. To prevent unrelated traffic and maintain proper asepsis, how should the operating room and its dressing room be positioned within the suite layout?
o: Operating room integrated into the outpatient day clinic; dressing room placed inside the central housekeeping hub.
Operating room as remote as practicable from the suite entrance; dressing room positioned to avoid clean staff exposure to dirty areas.
Operating room flanking the public corridor; dressing room shared directly with the service zone loading dock.
Operating room positioned directly at the entrance gate; dressing room opening out to the public elevator lobby.
questions.n: This layout protects the sterile core by keeping the operating room clear of cross-traffic and using the dressing room as a secure, clean transition point.

questions.q: To achieve the mandated healthy and aesthetic environment within the Deep Zone—specifically inside major operating theaters—what wall color palette should the architect specify, and why?
o: Deep crimson or terracotta; reduces the high visual contrast caused by blood splatters on clean surfaces.
Pure stark white; reflects maximum light to ensure absolute visibility and detect any surface dust particles.
Pale green or blue-green; complements the color of human blood to reduce eye fatigue and eliminate after-images for surgeons.
Bright energetic yellow; stimulates awareness and prevents drowsiness among staff during extended procedures.
questions.n: Green and blue-green tones neutralize the visual fatigue caused by focusing on red blood tissue, helping surgeons maintain focus and precision.

questions.q: The administrative services and main admitting office are located in the high-stress Outer Zone near the entrance. What color scheme is most appropriate here to promote patient comfort?
o: Monolithic industrial greys; projects an image of corporate efficiency, high-tech organization, and modern authority.
High-contrast primary gloss pigments; provides strong, vibrant stimulation to speed up patient registration and administrative transactions.
Saturated dark violet; induces deep sedation and limits behavioral outbursts in public waiting areas.
Soft, warm neutrals or muted earth tones; creates a welcoming, low-stress environment that helps reduce patient anxiety upon entry.
questions.n: Warm, muted earth tones create a calming, non-institutional atmosphere that helps ease anxiety for arriving patients.

questions.q: A pediatric inpatient ward requires an environment that actively balances rest with positive distraction. How should the architect plan the color application across the walls and signage graphics?
o: Calming pastel backdrops on primary walls to promote rest, with a clear system of cheerful, high-contrast accent colors on signage for clear orientation.
Monochromatic neon backdrops with matching translucent signage text overlays.
Saturated, multi-colored geometric patterns across all walls to create an energetic, stimulating playground theme.
Uniform dark olive tones across both walls and signage to minimize maintenance needs and hide scuff marks.
questions.n: This layout uses soft, calming pastels on large wall surfaces to encourage rest, while using bright, high-contrast colors on signage to help children navigate the space easily.
